newsitem.title: GERMANY: Audi seeks to keep positive course in 97.
newsitem.headline: Audi seeks to keep positive course in 97.

text.p: Audi AG, the luxury carmaker unit of Volkswagen AG, said on Tuesday it hoped to be able to keep up its growth in 1997 and planned to add new models in the premium market in the coming years.

"We assume that we will be able to maintain our positive course in 1997," incoming Audi management board chairman Franz-Josef Paefgen said in the text of a speech at the carmaker's annual news conference.

"We expect 1997 to be another successful year for us. The results of the first two months of this year confirm that we are right in our assumption," he said, noting a 15 percent increase in group sales to 3.32 billion marks for January and February.
Audi seeks to keep positive course in 97
But he said the figures for the first two months should not give rise to "exaggerated expectations" for 1997 as a whole.
"The availability of individual models due to restricted production capacities sets certain limits to volume growth," Paefgen said.

But Paefgen said Audi would be able to surpass the 500,000 unit level in terms of customer deliveries in 1997 after Audi reported a 9.9 percent increase in 1996 customer deliveries to 492,096 units, in part due to the launch of the new A6 saloon.
"The A6 will give our sales an additional push in the right direction," he said.

Paefgen, who will succeed Herbert Demel as management board chairman on July 1, said Audi was not interested in achieving "spectacular success" in the short term but in creating long-term growth potential.

"We will continue to strengthen our position in the premium segment in the next few years with additional new products," Paefgen said. "We will continue to improve our brand image and promote globalisation."
Audi also said it anticipates a further rise sales and earnings in 1997 and that its pre-tax profit margin will be at least as high as 1996.
The carmaker added it planned for six billion marks ($3.5 billion) in investments through 2000 and that it planned to add models in the premium market segment.
